source.publication: 2025 Complete Income Tax Instruction Booklet (ip25), Kansas Department of Revenue, with Form K-40 and Schedule S bound in (PDF pages 19-22)
source.section: Form K-40 lines 1-12 (ip25 PDF page 20; exemption block PDF page 19); K-40 instructions lines 1-3 (PDF page 6), line 4 and exemptions (PDF page 6), lines 5-8 (PDF page 7); WORKSHEET - Standard Deduction for People 65 or Older and/or Blind (PDF page 6); tax rate schedule: 2025 Tax Computation Worksheet (PDF page 34) and Tax Table (PDF pages 27-34)

worked: Federal AGI = IRA distribution (you) 50,000.00 + IRA distribution (spouse) 20,000.00 = 70,000.00. Federal taxable income = 70,000.00 - standard deduction 34,700.00 (31,500.00 + 2 x 1,600.00 for 65 or older) = 35,300.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Kansas starts from federal AGI). No Kansas modifications: Schedule S lines A9 and A26 are 0.00, line A27 net modification 0.00 (the K-40 instructions let a filer skip line 2). Form K-40: line 1 federal AGI 70,000.00; line 2 modifications 0.00; line 3 Kansas AGI = 70,000.00 + (0.00) = 70,000.00; line 4 standard deduction (married filing joint), worksheet for people 65 or older: 2 boxes checked (you and spouse), 8,240.00 + 2 x 700.00 = 9,640.00 (the worksheet prints 9,640.00); line 5 exemption allowance (2 exemptions) 18,320.00, 0 dependents; line 6 total deductions = 9,640.00 + 18,320.00 = 27,960.00; line 7 taxable income = 70,000.00 - 27,960.00 = 42,040.00; line 8 tax (rate schedule as numbers, PDF page 34): 5.2% x 42,040.00 = 2,186.0800 = 2,186.08. Line 7 is 100,000 or less, so the form reads the tax table: row 42,001-42,050, married filing joint column, PDF page 30, gives 2,185; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 9-10 do not apply (resident); line 11 0.00; line 12 total income tax 2,186.08. Credits (lines 13-15, 17): none, 0.00; state income tax = 2,186.08.
accepted_approximations: A pension from another state's government, private pensions, IRA and other employer-plan distributions and Roth conversions stay in Kansas income: no line subtracts them. This is read from the booklet's silence, not from a sentence saying they are taxed.
Tax is computed from the rates, not the printed tables and rounded worksheet subtraction.
